Daimon details a tactile-data pipeline for industrial manipulation

A new interview explains 30 Hz tactile feedback, simulation calibration and limits of transferring skills into production.

The Robot Report ↗19 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2Videos 1

Infrastructure for contact-aware robots

In an interview published October 19, Daimon Robotics described sensors, collection devices, simulation and evaluation tools intended to support robot-model developers. This is a new disclosure of its approach and deployment status, not an announcement of a newly launched sensor.

Making contact data useful for training

The company describes 30 Hz feedback and calibrating simulations with measured physical properties such as friction and contact forces, which cameras alone cannot fully capture. It discussed more than 10,000 hours of data, while its longer-term Daimon-Infinity initiative targets over one million hours. That target should not be treated as a delivered dataset.

Demonstrations and production evidence

Examples discussed include bracelet threading, work on tote bags and collecting broken glass, with the Umi device collecting human interaction data. Daimon reports industrial assembly and warehouse work but withholds customer names under nondisclosure agreements. It also acknowledges limited model generalization, leaving production reliability to be demonstrated through measured results.
